claims.text: The target Ta-based refractory alloy is a disordered BCC solid solution at 0 K.
Ta-based refractory BCC HEAs exhibit significant atomic-size mismatch and associated local lattice distortion.
An MLP-based perturbation scheme trained on disordered reference states can predict the melting free energy with less than 5% error.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture complex multicomponent liquid structure and local chemical ordering.
The structural errors of standard EAM potentials systematically overestimate melting temperature.
Near melting, complex multicomponent interactions dominate the liquid behavior of the target refractory HEA.
Local lattice distortion and short-range chemical ordering are important structural features of the liquid phase.
Training on disordered configurations, liquid snapshots, and local-distortion descriptors enables the MLP to capture those liquid structural features.
A model using Holder means and other elemental or structural properties predicted the shear and bulk moduli of NbTaTiV with relative errors of 2.5% and 6%, respectively.
An MLP can learn the disordered liquid potential-energy surface by interpolating among training configurations containing local-distortion effects.
Learning that potential-energy surface allows accurate solid–liquid free-energy differences to be obtained without DFT sampling of the full phase space.
EAM potentials give incorrect solid–liquid entropy and enthalpy balances because their pairwise or simple many-body forms cannot represent the relevant multicomponent liquid structure.
The proposed MLP scheme will predict melting temperature within 5% of experiment or a high-fidelity DFT benchmark.
Standard EAM predictions of melting temperature will deviate by more than 10%.
The proposed perturbation scheme will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.
First-principles approaches are computationally expensive and consequently restrict accessible simulation sizes.
The proposed method may fail when strong chemical ordering or Laves-phase precursors lie outside the MLP training set.
MLP accuracy depends strongly on including liquid-like and highly distorted disordered configurations in the training set.
Training biased toward ordered compounds may give unreliable predictions for a disordered liquid.
The cited evidence does not characterize specific TOR-TILD failure modes in multicomponent composition spaces.
